sentences.text: 2. Injured/claimant aged 40 years, working as an Assistant Teacher in Government school, met with an accident on 01.08.2014 and filed a claim petition claiming compensation of Rs.15,00,000/-.
The Tribunal after considering entire material on record, granted an amount of Rs.84,585/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till realization.

3. Aggrieved by the said order, the injured/claimant preferred this appeal in which it is contended that, meager amounts are granted for pain and suffering, loss of amenities and also medical expenses and NC: 2025:KHC-K:7487 HC-KAR no amounts granted for other heads.
Thus, requested for enhancement of the compensation.

4. Insurance company also preferred this appeal in which it is contended that, the Insurance Company has issued notice to the owner of the vehicle and requested him to furnish the copy of driving licence, but, he failed to do so.
As such, an adverse inference was drawn against him for violation of terms and conditions of the policy.
Thus, requested for pay and recovery.
5. It is further contended by the Insurance Company that, appellant has not examined the doctor to show that she sustained grievous injuries.
Further, though there are no medical documents to show her medical expenses to an extent of Rs.33,585, the Tribunal erred in granting the said amount.
Therefore, requested for modification of the order.
6. Heard the arguments of both sides.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:7487 HC-KAR 7.
Appellant/claimant was aged 40 years, working as Assistant Teacher in Government School in Malghan and getting a salary of Rs.28,944/- per month.
But, the salary slip is not filed before the Court to prove her income.
She met with an accident on 01.08.2014, therefore, this Court finds it reasonable to take her notional income as Rs.7,500/- per month, as per the guidelines of Karnataka Legal Services Authority.
She was hospitalized for 2 days and she filed the medical bills under Ex.P5 for an amount of Rs.33,585/-.

As per the Wound Certificate, filed under Ex.P5, claimant sustained dentoavelor fracture of upper anterior teeth and other injuries over face, on upper and lower lip,
chin, near left eye, on head, left knee and on other parts of the body, which are grievous in nature.
As per discharge summary - Ex.P7, she was admitted on 01.08.2014 and discharged on 03.08.2014.
She has sustained injury over face on upper and lower limb.
Appellant/claimant has not examined the NC: 2025:KHC-K:7487 HC-KAR doctor, as such, the question of assessing the disability or granting future earning capacity does not arise.
8. In view of the above discussion, considering the nature of injuries, this Court finds it reasonable to award an amount of Rs.22,000/- under the head Injuries.

9. The Tribunal granted Rs.40,000/- for pain and suffering, Rs.10,000/- for loss of amenities and Rs.33,585/- for medical expenses and it needs no interference and this Court finds it reasonable to The Manager, Reliance vs Manjula And Anr on 4 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/25670945/

sentences.text: 4 grant an amount of Rs.30,000/- for extra nourishment, transportation and attended charges.

10. She might not have attended any other work at least for a period of two months, therefore,
Rs.15,000/- (7,500 x 2) towards loss of income during laid up period.
11.
In all, the total compensation comes to Rs.1,50,585/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:7487 HC-KAR 12.
The Tribunal held that respondent Nos.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation and directed the Insurance Company to deposit the amount.
But as per the contention of the Insurance Company, there is no driving license, as such, no amount was deposited till today.
Hence, this Court finds it reasonable to direct the Insurance Company to deposit the compensation with interest.

13. The compensation awarded by the Tribunal is modified as under:
 Heads Amount in Rs.
 1. Injuries 22,000/-
 2. Pain and suffering 40,000/-
 3. Loss of amenities 10,000/-
 4. Medical expenses 33,585/-
 5.Transportation, extra 30,000/-
 nourishment and attendant  charges  6. Loss of earning during laid up 15,000/-
 period for two months

Total 1,50,585/-
 NC: 2025:KHC-K:7487 HC-KAR

Accordingly, the appellant is entitled for a total compensation of Rs.1,50,585/- as against Rs.84,585/-.
14.

In the result, the following order is passed:
i) Both appeals are partly allowed;

iii) Insurance Company is directed to deposit Rs.1,50,585/- with interest at the rate of 6% within 1 month from the date of this order and at liberty to recover the same from the owner of the vehicle.
iv) On such deposit, claimant/appellant is permitted to withdraw the entire amount along with interest accrued on it.
